## Purpose

This SOP describes procedures for the manual collection, preservation,
and handling of surface water samples. Representative samples are
required for defensible water quality data [@apha2012;
@usepa2014fieldsampling].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Manual collection of surface water samples from
  streams, rivers, lakes, ponds, lagoons, surface impoundments,
  wastewater access points, and outfalls
- **Does not apply to:** Automated sampling devices, pelagic marine
  sampling, or groundwater sampling
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve sampling plan, ensure training compliance       |
| Field Lead        | Coordinate logistics, verify equipment and supplies     |
| Trained Personnel | Collect and handle samples per this SOP                 |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent sampling           |

### Required Training

- [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)
- [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
  (for sample preservation chemicals)


## Definitions

- **Bailer:** A cylindrical sampling device lowered on a line to
  collect water at a specific depth; commonly used in wells and deep
  water; can be disposable (polyethylene) or reusable (stainless
  steel).
- **Bottle blank:** A sample container filled with laboratory-pure
  water, preserved identically to field samples, and submitted to the
  laboratory as a QC sample to detect contamination from the container
  or washing process [@apha2012].
- **Chain of custody (COC):** A legal record of sample possession at
  every transfer point from collection to analysis; must accompany all
  samples; see [SOP-F008](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd)
  for the full procedure [@usepa2014fieldsampling].
- **Discrete-depth sampler:** A device (Van Dorn, Kemmerer bottle) that
  collects a water sample from a specific depth without mixing with
  overlying or underlying water; tripped by a messenger weight.
- **Equipment blank:** Laboratory-pure water poured through or into
  sampling equipment in the field, collected and analyzed as a QC
  sample to verify equipment cleanliness.
- **Field duplicate:** A second sample collected at the same time and
  location as a primary sample and submitted blind to the laboratory;
  used to assess field and laboratory precision.
- **Grab sample:** A single-point, instantaneous water sample collected
  at one time and place; represents conditions at that moment only; the
  simplest and most common field collection method [@apha2012].
- **Holding time:** The maximum elapsed time between sample collection
  and analysis within which the sample remains analytically valid;
  analyte- and preservative-specific (e.g., 6 h for E. coli, 28 d for
  nitrate preserved with H~2~SO~4~) [@apha2012].
- **Peristaltic pump:** A battery-operated field sampling pump that
  moves sample water through disposable tubing by compressing the tube
  with rollers; used to collect samples from depths or locations
  inaccessible by hand.
- **Preservative:** A chemical added to a sample container to retard
  biological or chemical degradation of target analytes during
  transport and storage (e.g., H~2~SO~4~ for nutrients, HNO~3~ for
  metals, Na~2~S~2~O~3~ for chlorine) [@apha2012].
- **Sampler blank:** Laboratory-pure water passed through or into a
  sampling device (bailer, peristaltic pump) and submitted as a QC
  sample to verify the device is clean.
- **Zero headspace:** A sample container filled completely with no air
  gap; required for volatile organic compound (VOC) samples to prevent
  analyte loss to the headspace.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Biological/Chemical:** Water bodies may be contaminated; avoid
  ingestion and direct skin contact.
- **Physical:** Drowning risk, slippery surfaces, swift currents,
  unstable banks, and bridge traffic.
- **Chemical:** Sample preservatives (H~2~SO~4~, HNO~3~, NaOH) in
  pre-preserved bottles are corrosive.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Latex or nitrile gloves
- [ ] Leather gloves (for handling ropes and cables)
- [ ] Antibacterial hand sanitizer or soap
- [ ] Personal flotation device (PFD) when sampling from boats or in
      deep/swift water
- [ ] Safety vest and lines (as appropriate for the site)
- [ ] Traffic control signs and cones (for bridge sampling)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for
emergency response procedures, including medical emergencies near
water.


## Summary of Collection Methods

Sampling situations vary widely and no universal procedure applies.
Representative samples from most surface waters can be collected by
one or more of the following:

- Bailers
- Dip samplers
- Direct method (hand collection)
- Discrete depth samplers (Kemmerer or Van Dorn bottles)
- Peristaltic pumps
- Stormwater collection devices

[@apha2012; @usepa2014fieldsampling]


## Required Materials

### Field Documentation

- Field notebook and pens (per
  [SOP-F003](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd))
- Chain of custody forms (per
  [SOP-F008](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd))
- Sample tags with assigned sample numbers
- Field data sheets

### Sampling Equipment

| Item                                   | Notes                                      |
|:---------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| 500 or 1000 mL sampling bottles        | Polypropylene or glass, as required by the analyte |
| Syringe filters (0.45 µm)              | For dissolved analyte samples              |
| Stainless steel or Teflon dipper       | For surface grab samples                   |
| Depth-integrated sampler               | For vertically integrated samples          |
| Van Dorn or Kemmerer sampler           | For discrete depth samples                 |
| Extension pole with container holder   | For sampling from piers, docks, or banks   |
| Deionized / ultrapure distilled water  | For blanks and equipment rinsing           |
| Decontamination supplies               | To prevent invasive species transfer       |

### Transport and Storage

| Item                          | Notes                                        |
|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------|
| Coolers with ice              | Pre-chilled to 4 °C                          |
| Pre-labeled sample containers | From the analytical lab, with preservatives  |
| Custody seals                 | For sealing coolers before shipment          |


## Interferences and Contamination Prevention

::: {.callout-important}
### Critical
The inner surfaces of sample bottles and caps must not be touched
with bare hands, gloves, or any other material. Keep sample bottles
in a clean environment away from dust, dirt, fumes, and vehicle
exhaust [@apha2012].
:::

- Collect samples upstream of your position and upstream of any
  sampling-related disturbance.
- Sample away from areas influenced by tributaries, outfalls, or other
  point sources unless those features are the target.
- Change gloves between sample sites to prevent cross-contamination.


## Procedure

### Field Collection -- Direct Method (Grab Sample)

1. Remove the stopper or lid from the container just before sampling.
2. Do not contaminate the cap, neck, or inside of the bottle.
3. **If no preservative is present:** Face upstream in flowing water
   (or upwind in still water). Hold the container near its base,
   reach out in front of your body, and plunge it mouth-down below the
   surface to approximately mid-water column.
4. If the water is too shallow for this technique (risk of disturbing
   sediment), collect a surface water sample and note the change of
   method in the field notebook.
5. Fill the bottle to the appropriate level for the target analyte.
6. Leave a small headspace for mixing, **except** for volatile organics
   and alkalinity samples (no headspace).

### Field Collection -- Extension Pole

1. Securely attach the sample container (lid in place) to the pole
   holder using clamps.
2. Remove the lid carefully to avoid contamination.
3. Follow the direct method procedure above.
4. Do not use this method for pre-preserved containers; use
   intermediate devices instead.

### Field Collection -- Pre-Preserved Containers

1. Hold the container upright.
2. Place the lid over the mouth to create a small opening.
3. Submerge and fill carefully to avoid spilling or diluting the
   preservative.

### Field Collection -- Intermediate Devices

For samples collected via Van Dorn, Kemmerer, bailer, or peristaltic
pump, follow the device operating instructions (see
[SOP-F202](SOP-F202-sontek-velocity-meters.qmd) for pump procedures).
Transfer collected water to appropriate labeled sample containers
promptly [@usepa2014fieldsampling].

::: {.callout-tip}
### Sampler Blanks
Prepare periodic sampler blanks by pouring ultrapure distilled water
through or into the sampler and submitting for laboratory analysis to
verify cleanliness [@apha2012].
:::


## Sample Preservation, Handling, and Storage {#sec-preservation}

Once samples are collected:

1. Transfer samples to correctly labeled containers.
2. Preserve immediately, or verify that pre-preserved bottles were
   used (see holding-time requirements, Table 9.1 in @apha2012).
3. Record all pertinent data in the field notebook and on the COC form.
4. Attach custody seals to the cooler before transport.
5. Decontaminate all sampling equipment before collecting additional
   samples (see [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd)).

::: {.callout-important}
Samples must never stand in the sun. Store on ice in coolers
immediately after collection and ship to the laboratory without delay
[@usepa2014fieldsampling].
:::


## Quality Control

### Bottle Blanks

Before each field trip, select one sample bottle per ten of each
container type, fill with ultrapure distilled water, preserve
identically to field samples, and submit for analysis as a "bottle
blank" [@apha2012].

### Field Duplicates

Collect one field duplicate per 10 samples (minimum one per event).
Duplicates are collected from the same location at the same time and
submitted blind to the laboratory.

### Equipment Blanks

When non-dedicated sampling equipment is used, collect an equipment
blank (ultrapure distilled water through the equipment) and submit
for analysis.

### Documentation

- Complete the COC form before samples leave the field.
- Record all deviations from this SOP in the field notebook.
- Photograph site conditions at each sampling location.

## Training Record

Before collecting surface water samples independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd), and
   [SOP-L003](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
   in full
2. Demonstrate correct grab sampling technique (contamination
   prevention, bottle handling)
3. Demonstrate proper use of pre-preserved containers and at least one
   intermediate device (bailer, Van Dorn, or pump)
4. Complete at least one supervised sampling event including COC
   completion and sample cooler packaging
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
